item.title: 3.0.0-alpha.12
item.description:
macOS 27 only · Build 119

Note

Contributing is easier now

AGENTS.md tells AI coding agents, and the people using them, how to contribute to Thaw. CODING_STANDARDS.md says how code and text are written here. Read both before you open a pull request, whether you write the change yourself or with an agent.

If an AI helps with your change, see the AI-assisted contributions section of our contribution guidelines first: you stay responsible for the change and must be able to explain it, and the tool's terms have to let you contribute its output.

Most of these fixes keep menu bar items where you put them when an app answers Thaw slowly or renames its icon. The rest tighten who thaw:// links answer to.

Changed

  • Thaw no longer moves your pointer to reorder menu bar items. When macOS declines a move, the item stays where it is. Before, Thaw dragged it with a simulated mouse drag, which could leave the pointer or the item stuck. By @camguillory in #1418.
  • thaw:// links are stricter about who they trust. A sender's developer team counts only when Apple vouches for it. An app signed some other way is approved by its own signature, so it can't claim a trusted team. Replies go only to the app that asked, checked by its signature. Before, any app that handled the same link could receive them. In Reduced Mode, thaw://hide-app and thaw://show-app need an app you allowed, since they change which apps stay hidden. thaw://toggle-hidden still works for anyone.
  • The known macOS 27 limitations are in the Hiding section now, behind an info button next to the hiding method, instead of a card at the top of Layout.

Fixed

Menu bar order

  • Icons Thaw can't read in time stay where they are. When an app answered Thaw too slowly, its icons were moved next to Thaw's icon, out of Hidden or Always Hidden, and sometimes past Thaw's icon.
  • Icons from an app that is slow to start at login keep their section. Until the app answers on time, its icons arrive under a placeholder name, and Thaw placed them in Visible as new items. OneDrive calls every icon "OneDrive" until its accounts load, so with Native hiding the whole app showed even when you had hidden it. Thaw now waits for a slow app to answer, and gives each OneDrive icon, left to right, the account you saved it under. Once OneDrive names its accounts, Thaw uses those names. Reported by @michaeljauk in #1416.
  • An icon that publishes no name of its own, like Stats' Disk icon, can be moved again. Thaw tied it to an old entry left behind by Thaw itself, so it stayed at the far end of the bar and pulled the app's other icons after it.
  • Droppy's menu bar icon can be moved while its player is showing. Thaw saved the move under an entry macOS doesn't use for that icon, so the icon snapped back.
  • Dragging an item across the Hidden divider moves only that item. The neighbours the drop pushed along used to change section too, and the item you dragged could stay behind when macOS renewed it during the drag. Fixed by @camguillory in #1411.
  • After a display change, Thaw leaves your items alone while it reads the Hidden divider on the wrong side of the Clock. It used to move them into Hidden, or save that order as yours. Fixed by @camguillory in #1407.

Menu bar and appearance

  • The menu bar shape hides when Mission Control opens and returns when it closes. Fixed by @Belligerently in #1425.
  • Opening a hidden item no longer keeps an auto-hiding menu bar on screen. Thaw shows the item before pressing it. Fixed by @cnicc in #1409.
  • An app that Native hiding keeps off the menu bar shows its app icon in the Thaw Bar and Layout. Before, they showed a generic window shape, and Thaw revealed the hidden item to take its picture. Reported by @lucifercraig12345-create in #1424. Fixed by @camguillory in #1408.
  • The Right margin works with the Split shape. The right half now ends that far from the screen edge, like the left half does with the Left margin. Before, the slider did nothing, and the right half ended close to the Clock's text. Reported by @jaimefordham in #1412.
  • Thaw stays responsive when the app in front stops answering. When Thaw reads where that app's menus end, it now stops waiting after a moment.

Profiles and icons

  • Updating all of a profile's settings and layout keeps its pre/post scripts. Fixed by @Belligerently in #1423.
  • A profile whose saved file is missing can be removed from the list. Fixed by @Belligerently in #1420.
  • A large picture chosen as an item's icon is saved at icon size. Before, Thaw kept the whole picture in its settings.

Updates

  • Switching between Alpha and Beta checks for updates right away. When Settings ran as a separate app, Thaw waited for its next daily check, so you had to press Check for Updates.

item.title: 3.0.0-alpha.11
item.description:
macOS 27 only · Build 118

Most of the fixes in this release harden security, and they come from findings in a CodeRabbit deep scan.

New

  • You can skip menu bar visibility recovery when a removed app blocks it. Thaw keeps the recovery records as backups and leaves Native hiding off.
  • Settings can use a pure black background in dark mode. Turn on "Black background in dark mode" in General if you have an OLED display. Light mode looks the same as before, and the sidebar, toolbar and rows keep their glass.

Changed

  • thaw://proxy-press needs settings access and an app you allowed, like thaw://set, since it presses another app's menu bar item.
  • thaw://toggle-thawbar needs settings access, like thaw://set and thaw://toggle, since it saves a setting.
  • thaw://dump-items needs settings access, and reports back only to the app that asked. It no longer opens web links.
  • An imported profile arrives with "Ask before restarting" on, and Thaw refuses a file with more than 100 profiles.
  • thawctl get says it can't return a value instead of sending a request whose reply goes nowhere. Read settings from the ThawCtl app or your own app's callback.
  • One "Hidden items" picker replaces the "Use Thaw Bar" and "Always show hidden items" switches. Choose On click, Thaw Bar or Always shown for each display and for the global template. Your saved choice carries over, and thaw://set works as before.

Fixed

  • Restored translations for menu bar controls, appearance, overflow and Zen Mode that had fallen back to English after labels or punctuation changed.
  • Items moved to Hidden by automatic overflow remain available in Layout and the Thaw Bar when Native hiding removes them from the menu bar.
  • The recovery warning no longer reports every failed restore as an unreadable Control Center setting.
  • Thaw no longer quits when a group folder's icon briefly has no window. On macOS 27 that happens after the menu bar rearranges, and Thaw read the placeholder number macOS gives such an icon as a window ID. Reported by @perlytiara in #1397.
  • Relaunch Now can't run commands hidden in the name of the folder Thaw is in.
  • An app you allowed to use thaw:// links is checked by its own signature, so another app can't borrow the permission by using the same name. An app allowed without a signing team is asked again when its code changes.
  • A shortcut with an impossible key code no longer makes Thaw quit, when a profile with one is applied or at the next launch. Thaw skips that shortcut.
  • Another app can't switch your profile by pretending a Focus started or ended. Thaw checks the Focus state itself before it switches.
  • Applying a profile no longer restarts menu bar apps without asking. With spacing set to ask first, the Profiles pane asks, and a profile applied from the menu, a shortcut, Shortcuts, a link, a Focus or a Space saves its spacing for when the apps next start.
  • The profile preview warns that applying will restart menu bar apps when the profile has its own spacing for the display you're on.
  • The profile preview shows when a profile only reorders items in a section, instead of saying nothing would change.
  • Timed rehide hides the section again even if you don't move the pointer after showing it with a shortcut or a click.
  • A system item's stand-in turned off while it was starting no longer keeps running.
  • When a Focus ends, Thaw switches to the current Space's profile if it has one, as it does at launch, rather than the display's.
  • thawctl set accepts the key=value form its help shows, such as thawctl set showOnHover=true.
  • An app you add by hand under Automation can use thaw:// links. It's pinned to its own signature, like an app you allow from the prompt, instead of being listed but always refused.
  • A Focus profile stays on when Thaw can't read the Focus state. Only the system reporting that the Focus ended switches back.
  • Your saved menu bar order holds when icons go missing or overflow. An icon that briefly disappears keeps its place, icons behind the overflow arrows keep their order while you edit Visible, Always Hidden keeps its items while it's turned off, and items a profile doesn't mention stay where they were.
  • The Thaw Bar draws an app's icon at menu bar size when it has no picture of the item yet, instead of nearly twice the height of the icons around it on a notched display. Reported by @eisaias2000 in #1401.
  • Focus, Sound and other items macOS shows only some of the time go back to their place in your layout when they reappear, instead of staying where macOS put them. This was one way the Visible order drifted during the day in Automatic arrangement. Reported by @michaeljauk in #1410.
  • Thaw can put your Visible order back when the bar has an item your layout doesn't name yet, such as Now Playing. That item stays where it is, and the others return to your order. Before, Thaw gave up after three tries. Reported by @michaeljauk in #1410.
  • thaw://move-item answers notApplied when the menu bar doesn't take a move to Visible. It used to answer moved once the order was saved. Reported by @michaeljauk in #1410.
  • You can move items to the right of Siri on macOS 27. macOS doesn't pin Siri, so Thaw no longer treats it as fixed or moves it back to the end.
  • Search lists the same items as Layout, including hidden items macOS isn't drawing at the moment, and no longer lists items from apps you quit.
  • Dragging an item inside Hidden keeps your Always Hidden items in Always Hidden while that section is turned off.
  • Dropping a Visible item back where it was keeps the saved place of Visible items that are off screen at that moment.
  • Clock, Control Center and other system items you put in Hidden stay there after you switch away from Standard hiding and back. Thaw used to forget their place the first time it checked the bar with Standard hiding off.
  • Moving an item no longer pushes its neighbours into Hidden or Always Hidden, and no longer moves the item you dropped it next to when two items shared a position.
  • Thaw can restore your Visible order after every item in front of the Hidden divider has moved across it. Before, some items got no place and stayed where they were.
  • The screen recording indicator no longer blinks on and off during full-screen video. Thaw re-read the strip behind the menu bar every 20 seconds, which macOS counts as recording the video. It now skips that while the bar is hidden, and reads again only when a window under the bar moved. Reported by @edhinnig in #1413.

Known issues

  • On macOS 27.0.1, videos in a browser can't go full screen, and the menu bar can stay on screen over full-screen apps. This is a macOS 27 bug, not one in Thaw. Quitting MenuBarAgent in Activity Monitor fixes it until it comes back. Reported by @deadcoder0904 in #1404.

item.title: 3.0.0-beta.4
item.description:
macOS 27 only · Build 117

Important

On macOS 27.0.1, don't ⌘-drag the microphone or screen recording indicator while it's showing.

macOS's own menu bar process gets stuck redrawing it and restarts a minute later, with or without Thaw running, and the menu bar can come back in a different order. macOS 27.2 doesn't have this problem, so updating macOS is the fix. Reported by Keylag.

New

  • Profiles can keep your layout changes. Each profile has a Layout section in Settings > Profiles. "Keep layout changes in this profile", on by default, saves your icon moves to the active profile. "Apply again when Thaw starts", off by default, puts the profile's saved layout back at every start instead. Suggested by Keylag. By @diazdesandi.
  • About links to Floe, the launcher from the same team. By @diazdesandi.
  • Experimental: four more glass finishes. Appearance offers Invert, Edge, Sheer and Dim next to Regular and Clear. Edge, Sheer and Dim follow the shade macOS gives your menu bar icons, so dark icons sit on light glass and light icons on dark glass. A finish macOS doesn't support falls back to the standard glass. By @diazdesandi.
  • More section divider styles. Besides None and Chevron, Settings > Layout > Section divider style offers Line, Dot, Slash and Custom, which draws an image you choose, like a custom Thaw icon. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw offers to show apps an older version hid. Earlier betas could leave an app switched off in System Settings > Menu Bar with no record, which looks the same as an app you switched off yourself. Once, when Settings opens, Thaw lists those apps with nothing selected, and shows only the ones you pick. By @diazdesandi.

Changed

  • What's New lists Stable, Beta and Alpha releases separately. It opens on the channel you're on, and the Experiments link at the bottom is gone. By @diazdesandi.
  • Main buttons and checkboxes are see-through gold, with dark or light text to match, in place of solid gold with a black label. That covers Continue, Done, Apply and the other main buttons, and the checkboxes in onboarding, Layout and the update prompt. By @diazdesandi.
  • Shape corners go from square to round on a slider. In Settings > Appearance, Corners replaces the Round and Square choice, so the shape can be anything in between. Looks you saved keep their ends. By @diazdesandi.
  • The menu bar shape is picked from tabs. In Settings > Appearance, None, Full, Split and Notch are tabs like the others in Settings, and what the selected shape does is written below them. By @diazdesandi.
  • About is simpler. The version, build and commit are on one line next to the copy button. The update channel and automatic updates are pills instead of menus, What's New, Report a Bug and ⋯ sit together in one bar, and Floe moved into the ⋯ menu. By @diazdesandi.
  • Short choices are pills. Item arrangement, the hiding method, the Thaw Bar's arrangement, and the border style and width in Appearance are pills you click instead of menus. By @diazdesandi.
  • Buttons in Settings and What's New are capsules, like the glass buttons in macOS's own apps, instead of rounded rectangles. By @diazdesandi.
  • The permissions window looks like the welcome screens. When a permission goes missing, the window that asks for it again is laid out like onboarding, with its cards two to a row. By @diazdesandi.
  • Appearance says when macOS's menu bar background covers your look. If "Show menu bar background" is on in System Settings > Menu Bar, Appearance says so and opens that page, in place of a note that always showed. By @diazdesandi.
  • Selected rows look the same everywhere. The Swap Bar's buttons use the same see-through gold as the search results, and the gold follows Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast. By @diazdesandi.
  • The search panel and Settings search use the sidebar's headings. Groups of results have the same small uppercase names as the sidebar's groups. By @diazdesandi.
  • The sidebar is reorganized. Thaw's everyday pages come first, from General to Shortcuts, then Profiles, Automation and Experiments under a small Modules heading, then Privacy and Troubleshooting under Manage, and About last. The selected page has a see-through gold fill, and the arrow keys move between pages. The sidebar can't be customized anymore, so every page stays in the same place and pages you had hidden are back. By @diazdesandi.
  • Shortcuts are split into tabs: Visibility, Menu Bar Items, Layout, Thaw Bar and, once you've saved a profile, Profiles. By @diazdesandi.
  • Layout shows one list at a time. Under the bars, tabs switch between Options, Groups, Spacers and Apple's Items. Spacers are no longer folded away, Replace Control Center items has its own tab, and settings you rarely change, such as the hiding method, are under Options. Searching for one of them opens its tab. Suggested by Keylag on Discord. By @diazdesandi.
  • Appearance and What's New use the same tabs. In Appearance, Light and Dark are pills and the fills inside and behind the shape are tabs, so one fill shows at a time. What's New switches between Stable, Beta and Alpha with tabs. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw Bar, Displays and Troubleshooting have tabs too. Thaw Bar keeps its preview on top, with tabs for this display, the look and the options for all displays. Displays has Spacing, Spaces and Wide Displays, and Troubleshooting has Diagnostics, Repair and Reset. A search result opens the tab that holds it. By @diazdesandi.
  • The welcome screens replay from the ⋯ menu on About, instead of Troubleshooting. By @diazdesandi.
  • Simple Mode fits on one page. It shows a preview of your sections, which you can turn off, then a few settings: launch at login, item arrangement, when items hide again, the Always Hidden section, the shortcut and automatic updates. Everything else keeps working and stays in the full window. By @diazdesandi.
  • The profile menu left the Settings toolbar. Switch profiles from Profiles, the Thaw menu or a shortcut. By @diazdesandi.
  • Profiles shows one profile at a time. Pick a profile in the list to see its shortcut, display, Space and Focus, and what applying it would change, on the page instead of in a sheet. Switching profiles by display or Space moved here from Automation. By @diazdesandi.
  • Two hiding methods instead of three. Standard now does what Everything did: it also hides Clock, Control Center and Siri when you put them in a hidden section. If you used Standard, those three now move with your other icons when Thaw puts your order back. By @diazdesandi.
  • Native hiding is no longer marked beta, and Replace Control Center items now is. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw handles a display change in one pass. When you plug in, unplug or rearrange displays, Thaw waits for the screens to settle, then updates spacing, switches to the display's profile, shows hidden items you always show, and takes new icon pictures, once each. On a newly connected display, those hidden items appear about 12 seconds later, once macOS has finished laying out the menu bar. By @diazdesandi.

Fixed

  • Your layout survives a restart or logout when a profile switches by display or Space. Starting Thaw applied that profile again and moved icons back to where the profile had them, such as an item you had dragged into Always Hidden. Thaw now keeps the menu bar as you left it when the same profile is still active. Reported by Keylag. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • A ⌘-drag into another section sticks the first time. Thaw could put the dragged icon back in its old section a few seconds after you dropped it, so you had to drag it again. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden items go away again quickly after Settings opens. Opening Settings briefly shows hidden items to take pictures of their icons. With many apps running, some, such as Stats, could stay on the bar for over 15 seconds. They now go away within about 3 seconds. By @diazdesandi.
  • Right-clicking a hidden item in the Thaw Bar opens its menu without showing the item, when the app supports it, and a menu that opens a little late is no longer opened a second time. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw won't click a menu bar item it can't place. Right before a click it checks the item's fresh position, and skips it if macOS has the item parked off the bar mid-rearrange, so the click can't land on a neighbor. Thaw also pauses if it starts clicking far more than a person would. By @diazdesandi.
  • ⌘-dragging the screen recording, camera or FaceTime indicator no longer scrambles the menu bar. Thaw used to open every section for the drag, even though these items can't go into one. Dragging an app's icon still opens them, except with the Native hiding method. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw leaves the screen sharing indicator wherever you drop it. It treated the indicator as one of the items fixed next to the Clock, so after you ⌘-dragged it elsewhere, Thaw rearranged the rest of the bar around it. By @diazdesandi.
  • With the Native hiding method, Thaw no longer switches hidden apps on and off to take pictures of their icons, and a ⌘-drag no longer switches them all back on. Each switch made macOS rebuild the menu bar, so icons jumped around, and the pictures were thrown away anyway. Hidden items keep the picture taken while they were shown. By @diazdesandi.
  • With the Native hiding method, opening and closing a section quickly no longer makes macOS redraw the menu bar over and over. Each open or close switches the hidden apps on or off in macOS's list, and macOS lays out the whole bar each time. Thaw now waits a moment between changes, sending only the latest, and holds them for a few seconds after macOS's menu bar process restarts. Reported by Keylag. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • The menu bar no longer flickers when an app starts in the background. An app that launches every few minutes, such as a helper or a scheduled sync, made the whole bar redraw each time it started. Now each app causes at most one redraw per session. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden items no longer flash into the menu bar while Thaw takes pictures of their icons, such as when Settings or the Thaw Bar opens. Thaw covers that part of the bar with a picture of how it looked, kept current with what is behind the bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw uses less memory when other apps read its menus. While no Thaw window is open, Thaw removes its unused Window menu, so launchers and accessibility tools that read app menus no longer make Thaw use extra memory. By @diazdesandi.
  • Layout says why Native hiding didn't start. When you choose Native and it can't start, the picker goes back to Standard as before, and now the reason shows under it. Reported by @gigecogary in #1368. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Alpha builds get betas too. Builds on the Alpha channel only looked for alphas, so they never offered beta.3. Now the next beta reaches you without changing the channel. Reported by @bondskin in #1366. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • The Time Machine item is named Time Machine, not Item-0, in tooltips, search and Layout. Reported by @Macador in #1333. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Clicking Thaw's icon at the very top of the screen closes the Thaw Bar. On macOS 27 the icon sits a few points below the top edge, so a click above it reopened the Thaw Bar instead of closing it, and counted as a click on an empty part of the menu bar. Reported by @n0tishaan in #1335. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • No more typing hitches with Thaw's icon turned off. Thaw kept re-adding its hidden icon every minute, and its memory grew each time. Reported by @TianfeiXu in #1369. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • No discolored band when Notification Center opens. A Clock click or the Notification Center shortcut no longer paints a cover over the bar, which showed as a strip of the wrong color. Reported by @jmstacey in #1337. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw keeps your sections after a relaunch in Manual arrangement. It used to move items you had placed in Layout, often all of them to Visible. Reported by @felixkaiser in #1367. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • A new app's icon goes where the New Items placeholder is. Moving New Items to Hidden or Always Hidden in Layout had no effect, and new apps' icons always showed up in Visible. Now they land in that section, next to the item the placeholder sits beside. Reported by @nickawilliams in #1370. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Replaced Control Center items are the right size in Layout's preview. With Replace Control Center items on, Thaw's own Focus, AirDrop and other items drew bigger in the preview than the rest, though the menu bar was fine. Reported by Keylag on Discord. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • The popped-out Layout editor takes a drop anywhere in a row. Like the Layout bars in Settings, it no longer needs the drop near the icons. Reported by Keylag on Discord. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • The Thaw Bar stays closed when Zen Mode ends. With Always show hidden items on and the Thaw Bar off, leaving Zen Mode, such as when screen sharing stops, could open the Thaw Bar. The hidden items now come back in the menu bar. Reported by Keylag on Discord. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Automatic update checks run without opening Settings. Thaw only started checking for updates once Settings had been opened, so it could go days without looking. With Check for updates automatically on, it now checks once a day from launch, and with notifications off, the update window shows itself. Reported by Keylag on Discord. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • The menu bar shape hides during Mission Control again. On macOS 27 an empty outline of your Appearance shape stayed across the top of the screen while Mission Control was open. Reported by @fateoffuriou in #1359. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden icons in Layout match the Visible ones. macOS draws each menu bar icon in black or white to suit the wallpaper behind it, so hidden icons could show up black next to white visible ones. Layout and the pop-out editor draw one-color icons in the row's own ink. By @diazdesandi.
  • The Rules result in Settings search is translated. Its description showed in English whatever your language. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hover waits while ⌘ is held. Hidden items don't show or hide during a ⌘-drag, so the bar doesn't rearrange while you move an icon. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hover shows hidden items again after a click in empty menu bar space. The click paused hover until the section was next hidden, so if you only reveal by hovering, hover stayed off until Thaw restarted. Hover comes back as soon as the pointer leaves the menu bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • With Native hiding, Layout says which hidden icons stay in the menu bar. macOS shows or hides an app as a whole, and with Native hiding an app stays visible while any of its icons is in Visible. Layout marks its Hidden and Always Hidden icons as shown with the app's other items, offers to move them together, and no longer dims Visible icons that are on the bar. Reported by @felixkaiser in #1367. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • A ⌘-drag in Manual arrangement only changes the sections of the icons it moves. After a drag, Thaw read every icon's stored position, and in Manual those are often out of date, so icons you didn't touch could change sections. Switching to Manual keeps the sections you set in Layout too. By @diazdesandi.
  • Apps whose menu bar icon macOS lists but doesn't describe show up in Layout. Some apps, such as ZeroTier, draw an icon that Thaw's scan couldn't see, so it never appeared in Layout or the Thaw Bar. Thaw now picks up an app's icon from the menu bar itself when the app shows one icon and describes none. By @diazdesandi.
  • Only one copy of Thaw runs at a time. Opening a second copy, such as a test build next to the release, used to start a second menu bar manager fighting the first. Thaw asks which copy to keep. By @diazdesandi.
  • Apps you switched off in System Settings > Menu Bar stay off when Thaw restarts. If such an app was also in Thaw's Hidden section, restarting Thaw switched it back on, with either hiding method. Thaw now only switches on apps it switched off itself, and if it can't read its record of them, it asks before setting that record aside instead of guessing. Reported by @Snowman833 in #1367. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • One app is no longer listed many times in Hidden or Always Hidden. When an app changed an icon's name, Thaw kept the old name as one more icon of that app. Reported by @felixkaiser in #1367. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • VoiceOver and other accessibility tools no longer crash Thaw on About. Reading the version line sent Thaw into a loop asking itself for the same label, until it crashed. By @diazdesandi.
  • Icons keep their pictures when a menu bar item changes width. When an item such as a network traffic meter grew or shrank, Thaw threw away its picture and the pictures of every icon to its right in Layout and the Thaw Bar until the next capture. Now it keeps the last picture and takes a new one once the icons settle. By @diazdesandi.
  • Settings no longer blinks when a page moves to the app. With Settings running in its own process, opening a page such as Layout closed the window about a second before the app's own Settings window appeared. Now the window stays until the new one is in front. By @diazdesandi.
  • Always show hidden items follows the menu bar to another display right away. When the active menu bar moved to another display, hidden items could take up to a second to show there. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw changes nothing when it can't read its record of the apps it hid. Layout locks the hiding method, says why and offers to set the record aside, then starts Native hiding again once you confirm. Restore Missing Items opens in that case too and lists every app switched off in System Settings, so you pick which ones to show. By @diazdesandi.
  • Native hiding no longer drops back to Standard when it can't find macOS's list of apps. Thaw now tells a missing list from one it can't read, and starts a new one. Reported by Let that sink in (neverthelessyo) on Discord. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw puts your layout back within seconds of launch. With two or more hidden apps not running yet, it waited a full minute first. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden icons keep their pictures after a relaunch. Layout and the Thaw Bar showed app icons for hidden items until you revealed them again. By @diazdesandi.
  • After a Mac restart, apps that start slowly keep their section. Their icon could come back in Visible, and with Native hiding stay on the menu bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • Opening a section shows your icons in their saved order. Thaw skipped putting the order back before most reveals, so a divider could sit in the wrong place and Hidden icons could open in Always Hidden. By @diazdesandi.
  • Connecting a display no longer relaunches your menu bar apps, including when it switches to a profile with different spacing. The new spacing is saved, and apps use it the next time they start, or right away with Reapply Spacing. By @diazdesandi.
  • A display's profile is applied once when you connect it. It ran a second time after the menu bar settled. By @diazdesandi.
  • Order and hiding work with a display below or beside your main one. Thaw took that display's menu bar for icons parked off the bar and kept moving them, and clicks, hints and tooltips could land in the wrong place. Reported by @joaofrgomes in #1367. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • Quick ⌘-drags inside Visible stick. Thaw could put the icons back in the saved order, which takes a few seconds to catch up. The order also holds after a profile apply or a layout reset. By @diazdesandi.
  • Dropping an icon at the far left of Hidden keeps it in Hidden. It could land in Always Hidden, a section you couldn't see during the drag. By @diazdesandi.
  • Section names are translated in Layout, VoiceOver and move errors. Reported by @SakuraWang6 in #1382. Fixed by @SakuraWang6 and @diazdesandi.
  • With a Focus filter on, Thaw keeps your layout at launch. It applied the profile that was active when you quit again, undoing your changes. By @diazdesandi.
  • Layout changes are saved to the right profile. If no profile matched at launch, a later display or Space switch could save your current arrangement into the profile it switched to. By @diazdesandi.
  • Right-clicking a hidden item no longer slows down its next left click. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden items stay hidden while Thaw takes their pictures on a crowded menu bar. With many apps running, the cover over the bar could go away before the pictures were done. By @diazdesandi.
  • Each display's menu bar shape takes a new picture only when its own bar changes. Any display's color change made every display retake one, and turning a shade-following finish back on kept the old shade. By @diazdesandi.
  • Icons you ⌘-drag with a section open keep their new order. They snapped back about a second after the section closed, and the old order came back after a relaunch. By @camguillory.
  • Clicking the top of a fullscreen app no longer opens hidden items or the Thaw Bar when another display shows its menu bar. By @camguillory.
  • No blank band over the menu bar when the Thaw Bar opens with an app whose icon is turned off in its own settings. Thaw kept showing that app's empty item to take its picture, which covered the app menus for about four seconds. By @camguillory.
  • Unplugging a display no longer scrambles your icons. Thaw put your order back while macOS was still laying out the bar, then saved the scrambled order. It now waits for the bar to go quiet first. By @camguillory.
  • Moving an icon into Visible no longer pauses for an app that's gone. If your saved order named an app that was removed or changed its identifier, such as Floe, Thaw waited three seconds for it on every move. By @diazdesandi.
  • On a MacBook with a notch, hidden items that don't fit open in the Thaw Bar. Thaw counted the space left of the notch as room for icons, but macOS never puts them there. So it showed Hidden in the menu bar, and macOS tucked the rest behind ». By @diazdesandi.
  • The Thaw Bar leaves out apps you switched off in System Settings › Menu Bar. macOS never draws them, but the Thaw Bar listed them with their app icons. Apps that Native hiding switched off still show. Reported in #1260. Fixed by @diazdesandi.
  • "Move items that don't fit into Hidden" moves the icons behind macOS's arrows. On macOS 27.0.1 those icons weren't counted as missing from the bar, so Thaw thought everything fit and left them behind the arrows. They now go to Hidden and open from the Thaw Bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • Icons that only macOS draws get the right position with several displays. Thaw could place such an icon on another display's bar or below the bar, so it couldn't take its picture or click it. By @diazdesandi.
  • Moving the menu bar to another display switches that display's profile and spacing again. With displays that keep the same arrangement, Thaw kept the previous display's profile and spacing. By @diazdesandi.

Known issues

  • On macOS 27.0.1, ⌘-dragging the microphone or screen recording indicator makes macOS's menu bar process restart about a minute later, with or without Thaw. Afterwards some icons can come back out of order; dragging them into place on the menu bar fixes it. The app doing the recording can crash too; OBS did in one report. A Control Center control such as Timers can stay missing after the restart; opening Edit Controls brings it back. macOS 27.2 doesn't have this problem. Reported by Keylag.
  • With about 240 apps running, Thaw can't read the whole menu bar in time, so icons can go missing from Layout for a moment or come back in a different order. Reported by @joaofrgomes in #1367.
  • Zoom and some other apps can't be hidden with the Native hiding method, because macOS's list in System Settings > Menu Bar has no entry for them. They stay on the menu bar.

item.title: 3.0.0-alpha.10
item.description:
macOS 27 only · Build 115

New

  • Moving an item from its menu says how it went. After a move from the Thaw Bar or search, a short message says where the item went, or that it didn't move. By @diazdesandi.
  • Move items with a thaw:// link. thaw://move-item puts one or more items into Visible, Hidden or Always Hidden, optionally right after another item, the same way a drop in Layout does. Apps need your approval in Automation first. See docs/URI_SCHEMES.md. By @diazdesandi.
  • Restart the menu bar from Settings. Tools › Troubleshooting has a Restart Menu Bar button for when the menu bar gets stuck, for example on top of full-screen apps. Your layout is kept, and Thaw relaunches afterward. By @diazdesandi.
  • Move several items at once in Layout. Command-click or Shift-click icons to select them, then drag any of them or right-click to move them all to another section in one go. Press Escape or click an empty spot to clear the selection. By @diazdesandi.

Removed

  • Thaw Bar Only is gone. It was already switched off, and its launcher icon, shortcut and stand-in icons went with it. Items you kept there are ordinary Hidden items. By @diazdesandi.

Changed

  • A move macOS ignores falls back sooner. When macOS doesn't act on a move, Thaw starts dragging the icon after 0.7 seconds instead of 1.2. By @diazdesandi.

Changed: Settings

  • Tools lists the resets before your layout backups. Layout backups moved to the bottom of the page, so Troubleshooting and Reset come first. By @diazdesandi.
  • Troubleshooting has two fewer buttons. "Reset Control Center" is gone: on macOS 27 it also erased your choices in System Settings > Menu Bar, and "Restore Missing Items" brings items back without deleting anything. "Quit and Clear Cache" is gone too: saved item pictures are now thrown away after every update, which is what that button was for. By @diazdesandi.
  • Search lists every section in menu bar order. The order buttons and the per-section switches under Menu bar search are gone. By @diazdesandi.
  • Privacy has no Turn Everything Off button. It switched off the two rows above it; turn those off directly. By @diazdesandi.
  • Allow an app for thaw:// links by choosing it. Automation > Other apps > Choose App… opens a file picker instead of asking for a bundle ID. By @diazdesandi.
  • Automation is one short page. Each row says what's set right now. Display and Space switching open in a sheet, and a script's timeout and on/off switch are in its ⋯ menu. By @diazdesandi.
  • Simple Mode has an All Settings button in the toolbar, so you don't have to find Simple Mode in the ⋯ menu to leave it. By @diazdesandi.
  • "Show an item when its icon changes" moved to Visibility and lost its cooldown slider. The same item can show itself again after 45 seconds, the old default. By @diazdesandi.
  • Spaces is part of Displays. The page is now Displays & Spaces, with This Space and All Spaces below the display settings. Links and searches for Spaces open it. By @diazdesandi.
  • Triggers moved to Automation. They're under "When an app runs", and links to Triggers open Automation. By @diazdesandi.
  • One choice for how a spacing change applies. "When spacing changes" asks first, restarts menu bar apps right away, or waits until they restart. It replaces a picker and a switch and keeps what you had set. "Save spacing to every profile" is a switch now too. By @diazdesandi.
  • The spacing sliders fill out from Default, so you can see whether you made spacing tighter or wider. By @diazdesandi.
  • The buttons in triggers and the Recovery window match the rest of Settings. By @diazdesandi.
  • The Nightly update channel is called Alpha, matching the version numbers it delivers. You stay on it. By @diazdesandi.

Fixed

  • The tint and shape step aside in every full-screen app. With the menu bar set to stay shown, they slid down onto the app's toolbar, or covered the menu bar items. Reported by @Parakeet709 in #1229. By @diazdesandi.
  • Switching profiles no longer turns off Always Hidden or "Move items that don't fit into Hidden". A profile saved before you turned them on switched them back off whenever a display or Space changed. A profile can still turn Always Hidden on. By @diazdesandi.
  • Zen Mode keeps hover from revealing hidden items until you turn it off. The lock came undone the next time a section hid, so Zen Mode seemed to do nothing. By @diazdesandi.
  • "Always show hidden items" stays on. On a display where it's turned on, hidden items no longer hide again after a few seconds, and moving the pointer to another display no longer shows or hides them. By @malash.
  • Moving an item lands where you put it more often. Before it moves an icon, Thaw checks that the icons around the new spot haven't moved, and it reads every saved position back from macOS. A move that didn't stick switches to dragging right away instead of waiting. By @diazdesandi.
  • Showing hidden items no longer reshuffles the visible ones. When a hidden item had ended up among your visible items, showing the hidden section also rewrote the position of every visible item, which could move icons like Wi-Fi. By @diazdesandi.
  • Moving an item into a hidden section sticks. Thaw waited for the icon to move while its section was hidden, gave up, and after two tries stopped saving its position. It now saves the position right away, and the icon takes it the next time the section is shown. By @diazdesandi.
  • An app with several icons keeps each one where you put it. One of Droppy's icons could be saved under an entry macOS doesn't use, so it slid back into Hidden. By @diazdesandi.
  • A ⌘-drag isn't undone by Thaw's next write. macOS saves every icon's position the moment a drag ends, and Thaw could overwrite that with what it had read just before. Thaw now leaves alone any position that changed since it last looked. By @diazdesandi.
  • Repairs no longer swap icons that were already in order, and hidden items moved back beside a divider keep the order you set instead of coming back reversed. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw leaves Clock, Control Center, Live Activities and the camera indicator to macOS, which places them itself, instead of saving positions macOS ignores. By @diazdesandi.
  • Two apps with the same saved position no longer swap places after a restart. macOS breaks the tie by which app started first; Thaw now gives them their own positions when it rewrites that part of the menu bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • A failed save can no longer wipe macOS's saved menu bar positions. When that file couldn't be read, Thaw wrote a new one in its place and lost every other item's position. Now it leaves the file alone. By @diazdesandi.
  • Turning on Always Hidden no longer sweeps your items into it. Its divider could appear on the wrong side of the Hidden divider and stay there, and the next ⌘-drag then moved every item past it into Always Hidden. Thaw now puts the dividers back in order and ignores them while they are out of order. By @diazdesandi.
  • Items you move stay put when Thaw restarts or a display changes. With a profile active, Thaw re-applied that profile's layout after every launch, display change and app restart, undoing anything you had moved since. It now applies a profile only when it switches to it. Reported in #1314. By @diazdesandi.
  • Showing Hidden no longer shuffles items that are already in place. With Always Hidden on, Thaw judged Hidden items against Always Hidden's divider while that section was closed, where macOS leaves the divider beside the Hidden one. It then moved every Hidden item, one by one, to where it already was. By @diazdesandi.
  • Showing a hidden section no longer rewrites positions that are already right. Thaw rewrote the spacing of every item in the section each time it was shown, which made macOS lay the bar out again. It now leaves them alone when they're already in order. By @diazdesandi.
  • A passing jumble no longer becomes your layout. Thaw saved the live order every few seconds, including the moment after a wake, a display change or an app adding an icon, and then kept putting that order back. It now waits until the menu bar has been settled for twelve seconds, which outlasts the rewrite macOS makes ten seconds after an icon appears. By @diazdesandi.
  • An app with several icons no longer sets off a chain of repairs. When macOS didn't move one of them, Thaw counted it as a failure, tried again on every reveal and re-spaced the items around it. When it can't tell whether a move worked, because the app has another icon or an item came or went meanwhile, Thaw now leaves that icon alone for a while. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw stops rearranging the menu bar on its own if its repairs keep going. When automatic passes write more than four times in 30 seconds while you're not using the menu bar, they pause for a minute. Using the menu bar ends the pause. By @diazdesandi.
  • Thaw no longer puts its dividers back in order while hiding is changing. macOS holds the menu bar's order still while it hides or shows items and for a few seconds after, so a fix written then was wasted or set off another one. Thaw now waits until the menu bar has settled. By @diazdesandi.
  • Using the menu bar stops Thaw's background tidying. Starting a ⌘-drag, opening an item from the Thaw Bar, search or a hint, or showing a hidden section now calls off any automatic repair Thaw had planned, instead of letting it run on a menu bar you just changed. A layout you're looking at while a section is shown is also never saved as your order. By @diazdesandi.
  • Rearranging your displays is handled like plugging one in. Thaw used to wait for the menu bar to settle only when the number of displays changed. Swapping a display, moving one in System Settings or picking another main display now gets the same wait, and Thaw doesn't save the order while an icon is still at the screen's left edge or above the menu bar. By @diazdesandi.
  • Hidden items stay hidden in Manual arrangement when an app starts. Each time an app with a menu bar icon launched or restarted, or a display changed, Thaw read every item's section from where macOS had last placed it, which could move all your Hidden items back into Visible. It now does that only once, when Thaw itself starts. Reported by @promonteiro89 in #1357. By @diazdesandi.
  • Icons that turn up late after login get sorted. Some apps add their menu bar icons a minute or more after you log in, and Thaw could miss them until something else changed. It now takes a quick look 20, 40, 60 and 90 seconds after it starts, and only does anything if the set of icons changed. By @diazdesandi.

macOS 26 only

Hey, we have a website! The docs, the changelog and the roadmap are at getthaw.app.

The feature release for macOS 26 that 2.0.0 promised. Items can move on their own when something happens, related items stay together in groups, Zen Mode closes the whole menu bar with one hotkey, and Simple Mode fits Settings on one page. Screen Recording is now optional. Six betas led here, and most of what changed after the first one came from your reports. The beta entries below have the detail.

After you update:

  1. Profiles, saved layouts and hotkeys carry over. There is nothing to redo.
  2. Trigger conditions other than battery and power stay off until you switch them on under Trigger Sources.
  3. If you'd rather Thaw never restarts apps for a spacing change, set When applying spacing to Wait until next restart in Settings > Displays.
  4. With Homebrew, use the thaw cask. thaw@beta is Thaw 3, which needs macOS 27. #1221
  5. If something looks wrong, open an issue.

New

Triggers

  • Items move when something happens. A trigger can react to battery level, power, an app, the network, a VPN, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, an audio device, a display, a time, a Focus, a place, Energy Mode, heat, the camera or microphone, a script, or another icon changing. Conditions can be combined, and an action can be reversed. By @alvst in #735 and #965.
  • Icon-change triggers can be strict or loose. Loose ignores tiny redraws, strict reacts to any change, and the editor shows the icon it compares against. #1006
  • A trigger can follow an external drive, so a drive's helper app shows while the drive is plugged in. Requested by @lucifercraig12345-create in #1053.

Layout

  • Groups keep related items together. They move and hide as one, even across sections.
  • Spacers add a gap of the width you choose, with an optional fill.
  • Sort a section A to Z from its heading in Layout. #936
  • Layout opens in its own window, and you can open an item straight from it. #985
  • Opened items can stay a while. An item you open from search or the Thaw Bar can stay up to 30 seconds after its menu closes. Set it under Settings > General > After revealing. #342

Modes and profiles

  • Zen Mode closes every section with one hotkey. Hovering, automatic reveals and blinking icons can't open them until you turn it off.
  • Simple Mode shows Settings as one page. Switch it off to get everything back.
  • A profile can follow a Space, the way it already follows a display, and each Space can have its own menu bar look.

Appearance

  • The Thaw Bar has its own shape, tint and border. Requested by @kn666 in #248.
  • A new wallpaper re-tints the menu bar right away, and the adaptive gradient uses the wallpaper's main colours instead of one average.

Smaller things

  • Blinking icons can show themselves. An item that asks for attention briefly opens its section. Off by default, under Advanced.
  • A hotkey for automatic rehiding. By @nightah in #665.
  • Thaw can stay out of the Dock while you show and hide items. Turn on "Hide Dock icon when toggling the menu bar" in General. #1128
  • Remove a display you no longer use from the Per Display list. #1054
  • A Tools pane gathers the troubleshooting helpers.
  • Logs are easier to send. Diagnostic logs rotate on their own, by @nk-tedo-001 in #974. When an automatic move fails, Thaw saves a report you can attach to an issue. #994

Changed

  • Screen Recording is optional. An item Thaw can't capture shows as its app's icon, so the Thaw Bar, Layout and search work without the permission. Turn on "Show app icons instead of live previews" and the recording indicator goes away. #1051
  • Thaw stays out of your way while it moves items. It waits until you stop using the mouse and keyboard, leaves the pointer where you put it, and stops instead of trying the same move again and again. Your own drags always go through.
  • Thaw asks before every automatic app restart when "Confirm before relaunching apps" is on, not only after a display change. #1098
  • Hidden icons refresh as often as the slider says. By @camguillory in #942.
  • Displays has one Per display section instead of a block for each display, and marks displays with their own settings as Custom. #1045
  • "Dev Mode Flags" is now "Trigger Sources".
  • Search, About and the welcome screens follow your text size.
  • More of Thaw is translated, Russian most of all. Help at crowdin.com/project/thaw.

Fixed

Spacing

  • Changing the spacing no longer makes Spotlight disappear until you restart the Mac. Fixed by @commanderk33n in #720.
  • Changing the spacing no longer quits system services that can't be started again, and an app that says no to quitting is left running. Reported by @wiper2 in #1070.
  • The spacing prompt stays away after you cancel it, and "Don't ask again" sticks. #1180

Order and moving

  • Applying a profile no longer pushes your visible items into Hidden. Reported by @nk-tedo-001 in #1027.
  • Reordering items in Hidden works again. #1074, #1102, #1133
  • Items you drop into Always Hidden stay there. #1190
  • New apps land at the "New items" spot, not next to the Thaw icon. #1069
  • A revealed item shows on the right side of the arrow. #1035
  • A move right after an app updates no longer snaps back. Reported by @Chamiu in #1058.
  • The iPhone Mirroring Live Activity can be moved. Reported by @mi3suuu.
  • The Thaw icon stays put when you reconnect a display on a Mac with a notch.
  • An item no longer gets stuck in one place after a rehide fails, and duplicate Control Center items on non-English Macs are cleaned up. Reported by @balaji-dutt in #1079 and #1080.
  • Thaw no longer freezes its item list because of a window left behind by an earlier Thaw. #1032

Menu bar and Thaw Bar

  • Clicking a menu like File no longer opens Hidden in apps such as Firefox. #1028
  • Scrolling on the Thaw icon opens Hidden. #1073
  • A quit app no longer leaves an icon in the Thaw Bar. #1149
  • The Thaw Bar shows the right icons on every display, light or dark, and keeps them. #1065, #1046
  • No empty gap at launch when the Thaw icon is switched off. #1043
  • Clicking one of Apple's own items opens its menu.
  • Thaw no longer acts on a menu bar macOS never finished drawing. Reported by @ppocass in #1060.

Settings and search

  • The search panel takes your first keystroke. #969
  • Typing in the Settings search no longer freezes Thaw, and adding a spacer no longer crashes it. Reported by @lucifercraig12345-create in #1055 and #1056.
  • The Smart rehide delay can be seen and changed. #1049

Memory and speed

  • Thaw's memory grows more slowly over days of uptime. It redraws only what changed and stops capturing while your displays sleep. If you still see it grow, please comment on #1129.
  • Icons refresh without slowing Thaw down, and a blink trigger watches only its own items.

item.title: 1.3.0-beta.1
item.description:
1.3.0-beta.1: Profiles & Reliability

This beta introduces Settings Profiles, allowing you to save and switch between different Thaw configurations. Profiles can be triggered automatically based on display changes or Focus modes.

New Features:

  • Settings Profiles: Save your entire Thaw configuration as a profile and switch between different setups instantly. Perfect for different workflows, presentations, or multi-monitor configurations.
    • Create, duplicate, rename, and delete profiles
    • Import and export profiles for backup or sharing
    • Update existing profiles with current layout, configuration, or both
    Thanks to @nightah for implementing this feature!
  • Display Auto-Switch: Assign profiles to specific displays. When you connect a display, its associated profile is automatically applied.
  • Focus Mode Integration: Switch profiles automatically when Focus modes activate. Add Thaw as a Focus Filter in System Settings → Focus → [Mode] → Focus Filters to assign a profile to each Focus mode. The previous profile is restored when the Focus mode deactivates.
  • Profile Hotkeys: Assign keyboard shortcuts to quickly switch between your favorite profiles.
  • New Items Badge: A draggable badge in Menu Bar Layout settings lets you control exactly where newly detected menu bar items will appear. Drag it to position new items to the left or right of existing icons.
  • Option-Click Always Hidden: New setting to toggle the always-hidden section with Option+click on empty menu bar space.
  • Icon Overflow for Notch Displays: Improved handling of menu bar items on MacBooks with a notch. Items that would be hidden behind the notch are now properly managed.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • App Menu Click-Through: Fixed issues where clicking on application menus (File, Edit, View, etc.) would incorrectly trigger Thaw's show-on-click, hover, or scroll behaviors. App menus now work reliably.
  • Event Monitor Recovery: Added automatic health checking and recovery for background event monitors. If mouse click detection stops working, Thaw now recovers automatically instead of requiring a restart.
  • Layout Bar Stability: Fixed items disappearing from the layout bar during reorder operations, after reset, or when new items appear.
  • New Items Badge Position: Fixed the badge jumping to incorrect positions when reordering other items around it. The badge now stays in place unless explicitly dragged.
  • IceBar Click Responsiveness: Reduced click jitter when interacting with items in the IceBar.
  • Context Menu Size: Fixed context menus appearing unexpectedly large in certain situations.
  • Secondary Display Support: Fixed right-click context menu not working on secondary displays.

This is a beta release. Please report any issues you encounter on GitHub.

1.2.0: Icon Management Evolved

Important Note: This release introduces significant improvements to how Thaw manages menu bar item positions. Your icon positions are now automatically saved and restored across app restarts. If you experience any issues with icon positioning, use the new "Reset Thaw" button in Advanced Settings to restore default settings.

New Features:

  • Icon Position Persistence: Thaw now remembers where your icons belong! Menu bar items are automatically restored to their saved sections (visible, hidden, or always-hidden) after app restarts or system reboots. No more manually re-sorting icons after logging in.
  • Custom Menu Bar Item Names: You can now rename any menu bar item with a custom name of your choice. Perfect for giving cryptic icons a more descriptive label or organizing your workflow.
  • Menu Bar Item Tooltips: Enable optional tooltips that appear when hovering over items in the actual menu bar. Know exactly what each icon represents without clicking.
  • URL Scheme Support: External tools like Raycast can now control Thaw via the thaw:// URL scheme. Toggle the Thaw Bar, show or hide sections, and more using custom commands.
  • Manual Application Menu Toggle: Added a configurable hotkey to manually toggle application menu visibility. Useful for presentations or when you need the full menu bar width temporarily.
  • Thaw Bar Hover Highlight: Items in the Thaw Bar now show a subtle background highlight when hovered, making it easier to identify which item you're about to interact with.
  • Conflicting Apps Detection: Thaw now detects when other menu bar management apps are running and warns you about potential conflicts.
  • Per-Display Settings: Configure "Always show hidden items" and Thaw Bar positioning independently for each connected display. Perfect for multi-monitor setups with different screen sizes or notch configurations.
  • Reset Thaw Button: A new reset button in Advanced Settings allows you to quickly restore all Thaw settings to their defaults when troubleshooting.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Startup Stability: Fixed the "icon parade" issue where icons would continuously shuffle for 10–15 seconds after login. Thaw now enters a settling period during startup to prevent premature rearrangement.
  • Multi-Icon App Support: Apps with multiple menu bar icons (such as Stats, Hammerspoon, and iStat Menus) now stay properly organized in their designated sections instead of gradually migrating to the visible menu bar over time.
  • Memory Optimizations: Reduced memory usage by skipping wallpaper captures when not needed, clearing stale caches when displays disconnect, and adding proper cleanup for background tasks.
  • Performance: Throttled mouse event handling and optimized image caching to reduce CPU usage and improve overall responsiveness.
  • Privacy: Added screen recording permission checks for tooltips and search features. These options are now hidden in settings when permissions are not granted.
  • Visual Refinements: Improved IceBar item highlight sizing with better corner radius and padding for a more modern appearance that matches macOS design language.
  • Same-Icon Differentiation: Fixed a bug where different apps sharing the same icon were conflated. Thaw now correctly identifies items by their source application.
  • Auto-Rehide Reliability: Improved the rehide logic to prevent items from staying visible longer than intended, and fixed cases where manual hide states could get stuck.

Localization:

Thaw now supports 17 languages with 100% completion! A huge thank you to our community contributors:

  • Bahasa Indonesia: by @volcbs
  • Čeština (Czech): new in this release
  • Deutsch: by @Mutzki13
  • Español: by @diazdesandi
  • Français: by @PipaCode
  • Italiano: by @zichichi
  • 日本語 (Japanese): new in this release
  • 한국어 (Korean): by @YuriHan
  • Magyar (Hungarian): by @johnnybakucz
  • Nederlands (Dutch): by @SeBr28
  • Polski (Polish): new in this release
  • Português (Brasil): new in this release
  • Русский (Russian): new in this release
  • 简体中文 (Chinese Simplified): by @PiCpo
  • 正體中文 (Chinese Traditional): by @7a6163
  • ภาษาไทย (Thai): by @priesdelly
  • Türkçe (Turkish): new in this release

Thank you to everyone who tested the beta versions and provided feedback that made this release possible!

item.title: 1.2.0-rc.4
item.description:
1.2.0-rc.4: Localization Refinement & Stability Improvements

  • Internationalization Updates:
    • Finalized Czech (CS) language updates for the 1.2.0 release cycle.
    • Updated Turkish (TR) translations.
  • Fixes:
    • Reverted "Robust Icon Position Handling" to address regression issues and maintain system stability while the feature is further refined.

1.1.0: Breaking the Ice

⚠️ Important Note: Due to essential internal changes in how Thaw manages menu bar items, your current icon positions will be reset to "Always Visible." I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience, but this manual re-adjustment is unavoidable to ensure future stability.

Localization Support:

Thaw is now available in 12 languages with 100% completion. A huge thank you to our community contributors:

  • Chinese (Simplified): by @PiCpo
  • Chinese (Traditional): by @7a6163
  • Dutch: by @SeBr28
  • French: by @PipaCode
  • German: by @Mutzki13
  • Hungarian: by @johnnybakucz
  • Indonesian: by @volcbs
  • Italian: by @zichichi
  • Korean: by @YuriHan
  • Spanish: by @diazdesandi
  • Thai: by @priesdelly

Changes and Fixes:

  • Multi-Monitor Support: Improved app menu hiding logic to correctly account for screen edges and active menu bars across multiple monitors.
  • Ultra-wide Monitor Fix: Resolved an issue where menu bar items were incorrectly included in calculations, which previously caused "Hidden" and Always Hidden" items to appear incorrectly on the left side of ultra-wide screens.
  • Refined Notch Detection: Implemented auxiliaryTopLeftArea for more accurate notch detection and added an option to enable the IceBar only on displays with a notch.
  • Immediate UI Updates: Menubar shapes (split/full) now update instantly when settings are changed, eliminating the previous 30-second delay.
  • Display-Specific Layouts: Fixed an issue where menu bar items from primary displays were incorrectly included in trailing path calculations for external monitors.
  • Performance Optimizations: Reduced CPU usage by debouncing image cache updates, adding polling delays, and skipping background timer tasks when panels are hidden.
  • Simplified Settings: Removed the redundant "temporary item delay" setting as the smart rehide logic now handles these cases automatically.
  • Thaw Bar Scaling Fix: Resolved a scaling issue in the Thaw Bar by clamping the menu bar content height and capping item height to ensure consistent rendering.
  • New Interaction: Added the ability to double-click directly on the menu bar to reveal the "Always Hidden" section.

1.0.0: The Official Release

Thaw has reached its first stable milestone! This release consolidates all the progress from the beta period into a polished, reliable menu bar manager.

Latest Improvements (since beta 4):

  • Enhanced Reliability: Stabilized HIDEventManager logic to prevent "show on hover" and "show on click" from stopping after repeated use and prevent saving chevron divider position which could leave Thaw in an unusable state.
  • UI Polish: Condensed the menu bar tooltip for a cleaner look and added explicit double-click instructions.
  • System Safety: Improved thread safety by synchronizing access to the cursor hide count.
  • Apple Menu Fix: Refined synthetic press offsets to ensure Thaw never accidentally triggers the Apple menu.

Highlights from the Journey to 1.0:

  • The Big Thaw: Successfully forked and rebranded with a new identity, app icon, and independent bundle ID (com.stonerl.Thaw).
  • Ice Migration: Built-in support to import your old settings and control item positions from Ice.
  • Advanced Control: Introduced "Double-Click to Reveal" for always-hidden items and "Smart Rehide" strategies.
  • Modern macOS Support: Optimized for stability on macOS 26.
  • Performance: Faster icon caching, display-aware state refreshing, and thread-safe operations.

Known Issues:

If you are currently on macOS 14 or 15, please be aware that Thaw currently has some known bugs regarding temporary icons in the floating Thaw bar.

I am actively investigating these issues and will release a fix as soon as possible. You can track the progress of this issue here: GitHub Issue #1.

Thank you for all the feedback during the beta period that made this release possible!
